purpose: One row per capability this skill claims. Each row carries the strongest defensible grade, why that grade and not a higher one, the evidence behind it, the dependency this repository does not ship, and what would raise the row. A reader who has the installed skill but not this repository can check every row against the command it names.

grade_legend.observed: a command was run and its output exists, or a file in this repository was read at a stated revision. For a shipped tool this is a statement about the tool, not about any target the tool was pointed at.
grade_legend.inferred: follows from an observation or from documented mechanism, with the reasoning step stated. The step itself was not executed.
grade_legend.unverified: assumed, or reported elsewhere and not reproduced here. Usable as a plan input, never as a premise for a stronger claim.

rules_applied.chain_rule: A claim is only as strong as the weakest link in its chain. A passing self-check of a shipped script never upgrades a step nobody executed.
rules_applied.unknown_rule: Missing coverage is reported as unknown, never as absence. A search that returned nothing is evidence about the search.
rules_applied.tool_versus_target: The behaviour of a shipped script is observed when it is run; the behaviour of a target is observed only when a target was run and a result recorded. No target sample is present in this tree, so no row here grades a target.

measurement_host.os_product_name_note: The registry ProductName still reads Windows 10 on this Windows 11 host. The build number is the reliable field. Observed in the probe's own OS row.

measurement_window.note: The repository was being written by other authors during this pass. Files appeared and were rewritten between the first read and the final write. Every citation in this file was produced inside one window in which a hash of every shipped script was taken before and after the run and did not change; the script_pins block below records that hash set. Structural facts about which files exist were re-measured at the end of the window and are recorded with their own timestamp, because they moved during the pass.

path_convention: %TEMP% stands for the session's temporary directory, which was used as the scratch area so that nothing was written into the repository. The literal path is not reproduced because it contains a real user profile name, which this repository's own identity rules treat as a leak. The generated fixtures live only in that scratch area; no test binary is committed.
script_pins_note: sha256_first16 is the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the file at the pinned size. It is a pin, not a full digest; a reader re-running these commands should confirm the byte size before expecting the same output. hwprobe.py was rewritten again after the window (27098 bytes), so its pin covers exactly the run quoted here and not the file as it stands later.

state_at_first_measurement.gate_output: python check_repo.py reported 11 problems whose unique targets were those three files, plus the note that the tracked-file leak gate skipped because this tree is not a git checkout.

state_at_remeasurement.gate_output: Every reference and script path now resolves: check_repo.py reports 1 problem, and it is the leak scan alone. check_routing.py reports RESULT=ok. With PYTHONIOENCODING unset on a GBK console, check_repo.py instead crashes with UnicodeEncodeError while printing a leak finding, so the gate's own verdict is unreachable on that console until the encoding is set.

tree_state_at_end_of_window.why_both_are_recorded: Files named by the entry point and the routing table were absent at 19:17 and present at 19:22. Any row that cited a missing file was re-graded against the later measurement, and the earlier state is kept because it is what a reader of the 19:17 revision would have seen.
